slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
If soil and climate are Bordeaux's stage, then grape varieties are its leading players. One of Bordeaux's greatest hallmarks is the "art of blending" — châteaux cleverly assemble different varieties according to vintage, terroir, and target style to create wines of complexity and balance.

Learning Objectives

🍇 Master the Six Classic Varieties

Characteristics of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc, and Muscadelle

🎨 Understand the Art of Blending

Learn the role and complementary relationship of each variety in a blend

🗺️ Recognise Variety–Appellation Pairings

Understand why the Left Bank leads with Cab Sauv and the Right Bank leads with Merlot

👃 Identify Flavour Characteristics

Learn the typical aromas, palate, and structure of each variety
slides.1.title: Red Grape Varieties
slides.1.subtitle: The Big Three: Cab Sauv · Merlot · Cab Franc
slides.2.title: 🍇 Cabernet Sauvignon
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Structural Backbone
slides.2.highlights.0.content: High tannins, high acidity, late-ripening — the backbone of Left Bank blends
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Ageing Potential
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Needs 5–15+ years of bottle age to reach its peak
slides.2.quiz.question: Why does Cabernet Sauvignon perform best on Bordeaux's Left Bank?
slides.2.quiz.options.0: The Left Bank has high rainfall, suited to early-ripening varieties
slides.2.quiz.options.1: Médoc's gravel, well-drained soils help this late-ripening variety reach full maturity and concentrate flavour
slides.2.quiz.options.2: The Left Bank is at higher latitude and has lower temperatures
slides.2.quiz.options.3: Cabernet Sauvignon can only grow on the Left Bank
slides.2.quiz.explanation: Médoc's gravel soils drain well and retain heat, helping the late-ripening Cab Sauv achieve full maturity. Lean soils also naturally reduce yields, concentrating flavour.
slides.3.title: 🍷 Merlot
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Supple and Rounded
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Early-ripening variety with silky tannins — the soul of Right Bank blends
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Approachable Style
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Plum and chocolate notes; enjoyable while young
slides.3.quiz.question: What are the key characteristics of the Merlot grape variety?
slides.3.quiz.options.0: High tannins, late-ripening, needs long ageing
slides.3.quiz.options.1: Supple and rounded, early-ripening, reaches drinking maturity sooner
slides.3.quiz.explanation: Merlot is an early-ripening variety with larger, thin-skinned berries. It has medium tannins, a supple rounded palate, and is approachable young — the core variety in Bordeaux Right Bank blends.
slides.4.title: 🌿 Cabernet Franc
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Elegant Floral Notes
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Violets are its hallmark; combines herbal and floral aromas with a refined style
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Blending Key
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Lifts acidity on the Right Bank; adds floral elegance on the Left Bank
slides.4.quiz.question: What is Cabernet Franc's most distinctive signature aroma?
slides.4.quiz.explanation: Cabernet Franc is most recognisable for its violet and raspberry aromas, alongside herbal spice notes. Its elegant, refined style makes it an important aromatic enhancer on the Right Bank.
slides.5.title: White Grape Varieties
slides.5.subtitle: The Three White Varieties: SB · Sémillon · Muscadelle
slides.6.title: 🤍 Sauvignon Blanc
slides.6.highlights.0.title: Crisp and Lively
slides.6.highlights.0.content: High acidity, citrus and grassy notes — the source of white wine backbone
slides.6.highlights.1.title: Distinctive Aromas
slides.6.highlights.1.content: Cut grass, guava, white currant — a direct and immediately recognisable style
slides.6.quiz.question: What is Sauvignon Blanc's most important contribution to Bordeaux white wine blends?
slides.6.quiz.options.0: Provides sweetness and a rounded body
slides.6.quiz.options.2: Provides the acid backbone and freshness
slides.6.quiz.explanation: Sauvignon Blanc is known for its high acidity and fresh citrus/grassy fruit character. It provides structure and a lively palate to blends — the main source of freshness in Bordeaux white wines.
slides.7.title: 🍯 Sémillon + 🌸 Muscadelle
slides.7.highlights.0.title: Sémillon
slides.7.highlights.0.content: Thin skin readily susceptible to noble rot — the soul of Sauternes; adds body in dry whites
slides.7.highlights.1.title: Muscadelle
slides.7.highlights.1.content: Used in small quantities; imparts delicate rose and orange-blossom floral layers
slides.7.quiz.question: What is the key reason Sémillon is the principal variety in Sauternes botrytised sweet wine?
slides.7.quiz.options.0: Its high acidity keeps the sweet wine fresh
slides.7.quiz.options.1: Its thin skin is readily infected by Botrytis cinerea, concentrating sugars and flavours
slides.7.quiz.options.2: Its late-ripening character allows greater sugar accumulation
slides.7.quiz.options.3: Its deep colour suits the golden hue of sweet wine
slides.7.quiz.explanation: Sémillon's thin skin makes it readily susceptible to noble rot (Botrytis cinerea), which causes water to evaporate and concentrates sugars, aromas, and flavours to an extraordinary degree — this is the material basis of the Sauternes/Barsac noble-rot sweet wine style.
slides.9.title: Blending and Identification
slides.9.subtitle: Blend Ratios · Style Spectrum · Quick Identification Tips
slides.10.title: Typical Blending Ratio Quick Reference
slides.10.highlights.0.title: Left Bank vs Right Bank
slides.10.highlights.0.content: Left Bank uses Cab Sauv as the backbone; Right Bank uses Merlot as the soul
slides.10.highlights.1.title: Memory Mnemonic
slides.10.highlights.1.content: Left = Cab structure · Right = Merlot softness; SB = crisp freshness · Sémillon = rich body
slides.10.quiz.question: Which grape variety dominates Right Bank Bordeaux wines?
slides.10.quiz.explanation: The Right Bank (Saint-Émilion, Pomerol, etc.) is led by Merlot, which typically accounts for 60–90% of the blend, producing wines that are supple, elegant, and approachable relatively young.
slides.12.title: Quick Comparison of Four Major Styles
slides.12.highlights.0.title: Quick Reference
slides.12.highlights.0.content: Use acidity, tannins, and drinking window to differentiate the four major Bordeaux styles
slides.13.title: How Does Vintage Climate Affect Blending Ratios?
slides.13.highlights.0.title: Warm Vintages
slides.13.highlights.0.content: Cab Sauv ripens better and its proportion can be increased; in whites, raise SB ratio to preserve freshness
slides.13.highlights.1.title: Cool Vintages
slides.13.highlights.1.content: Merlot's earlier ripening gives it an advantage; Cab Franc provides acidity support
slides.14.title: Variety Identification: Smelling Steps and Aroma Quick Reference
slides.14.highlights.0.title: Step-by-Step Nosing
slides.14.highlights.0.content: Undisturbed → swirl → close nose; progressively decode layers of aroma
slides.14.highlights.1.title: Aroma → Variety
slides.14.highlights.1.content: Blackcurrant + herbal → CS; plum + chocolate → Merlot; violet → Cab Franc
slides.15.title: ⚠️ Common Confusions Quickly Clarified
slides.15.highlights.0.title: Variety ≠ Absolute Style
slides.15.highlights.0.content: Varietal character is a tendency; climate, ripeness, and winemaking determine the final expression
slides.15.quiz.question: Which of the following pairings best describes the typical style of a Right Bank red wine?
slides.15.quiz.options.0: High tannins + blackcurrant + late-ripening, needs long ageing
slides.15.quiz.options.1: Medium tannins + plum and red fruit + drinks relatively young
slides.15.quiz.options.2: High acidity + grassy citrus + crisp palate
slides.15.quiz.options.3: Honey and dried apricot + rich sweetness + long ageing capacity
slides.15.quiz.explanation: The Right Bank is led by Merlot, with plum and red fruit notes, supple silky tannins, and an earlier drinking window. High tannins and long ageing are hallmarks of Left Bank Cab Sauv-dominated wines.
slides.16.title: Lesson Complete
slides.16.description: Congratulations on completing the study of Bordeaux's principal grape varieties! You have mastered the characteristics of the six key varieties, aroma identification techniques, and the logic behind Left and Right Bank blending ratios.
